title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned La Sala, an exhibition hang. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: La Sala
options.lineage: museum hang and catalogue raisonné, Prado-style painted walls
options.thesis: Her work hung as a curated exhibition: every piece labelled with medium, scope and provenance you can check.
options.viewport: The exhibition title (her name) in wall vinyl, her portrait hung spotlit as the first work with its wall label naming the four rooms: Full-stack, Mobile, Web3, AI-driven engineering; the next room's first plate visible at the edge.
options.risk: Tips into stuffy old-master if the type turns classical; it must read as a contemporary hang, not a Baroque gallery.

raised.raise: Every plate, label and title sits on one hanging line and module; nothing floats.
Light belongs only to the work in focus; the rest of the room falls back to wall colour.
Every object on the wall carries a label at the same size; no label outranks another.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: one enormous wall title, everything else at label size.

options.label: Contact Sheet
options.thesis: The portfolio as a contact sheet: every frame shown, the selects circled in grease pencil.
options.viewport: A sheet of film strips (her portrait frames, then project frames); the select circled, a loupe magnifying her name and the four areas.
options.risk: Familiar: film-strip and darkroom motifs are common on creative portfolios.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Four lines, one board: every project and role departs on its platform, status live.
options.viewport: The board flips in her name; four platform columns for Full-stack, Mobile, Web3 and AI; rows are projects with live status (Marine Wobbles: in development).
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on scanability, but frames her as a timetable rather than a body of work: holds clarity, loses identification.
options.risk: Split-flap is a known novelty effect; reads as a gimmick if the cascade is the whole idea.

options.label: The Issue
options.thesis: Each area an issue of one magazine: strict two-column grid, one spot colour per issue, her mark hidden once per view.
options.viewport: A cover: serif masthead with her name, the current issue's spot colour, an oversized drop initial opening the four-area contents.
options.case: The strict grid makes the four areas legible as four issues; loses identification, since recruiters don't read a developer as a magazine.
options.risk: Editorial serif and heavy rules sit close to a common AI look, and it needs commissioned illustration that doesn't exist.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: Each project as a numbered assembly step.
options.viewport: Step 1: a parts inventory of her stack.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too playful for recruiters, and sky-blue pages break the dark-only commitment.
options.kept: One module grid that every element aligns to.

options.label: Night Sea
options.thesis: Pointer wakes light up a black sea.
options.viewport: Black field, glowing wake under the pointer.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an effect that competes with reading, and near-black with neon is the AI default look.
options.kept: Light marks only what is active; darkness reclaims the rest.

options.label: Cutaway Town
options.thesis: Each project a building with its wall removed.
options.viewport: A labelled town of her projects.
options.case: Fuses poorly: childlike and light-ground, against both the audience and the dark-only commitment.
options.kept: Every object wears a label at one constant size.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Her name as a live type specimen.
options.viewport: A giant morphing letter and axis readouts.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a type designer's world, not a developer's, and it says nothing about her four areas.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer portfolio as the category ships it, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role headline, short intro, buttons, then a grid of project cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other developer portfolios by design.
